answer: Proof of timestamping anchors a document's hash into a public blockchain through a Merkle tree, so anyone can later verify the document existed at or before that block. An orchard of documents can share one anchor, a hollow claim of an earlier date collapses because the hash was not in the tree then, and a thread of hashes links the document to the block header. A farm cannot backdate thousands of fake identities, because each timestamp requires a real on-chain anchor at that time, and rewriting history would mean rewriting the chain itself.
